settings.text: Poufs are some of the most versatile pieces of furniture around. These multi-functional marvels can serve as a footrest or extra seating, while also adding texture and a splash of colour to your spaces.

settings.heading: What are poufs and how can you use them?

settings.text:
Poufs are soft, multifunctional pieces of furniture that bring both practicality and charm to any room. Whether you’re decorating a spacious living area or making the most of a smaller flat, poufs offer a simple yet stylish solution.

So, what are poufs used for? They’re versatile home accessories often used as footstools, extra seating, or even as small side tables when topped with a tray. Their lightweight design and variety of styles make them ideal for both modern and traditional interiors.

In the living room, poufs can serve many purposes:

  • Place one in front of a sofa or armchair to rest your feet
  • Use several as casual seating for guests
  • Select square poufs or poufs with storage to combine design and functionality in smaller spaces

Whether you’re after flexibility or a decorative touch, poufs for the living room add comfort without taking up too much room.

How to style poufs in your living room

Poufs are a subtle but impactful way to complete your interior design. With the right style, fabric, or colour, they can either blend in or become a standout piece. If practicality is a priority, living room poufs with storage offer a smart solution for keeping everyday items like throws or magazines out of sight. Square poufs are especially suitable for more modern or minimalistic spaces, providing a clean, structured feel.

• Drape a throw over the pouf for added warmth and texture
  • Stack a couple of coffee table books on top for a styled, lived-in look
  • Add a tray to turn your pouf into a practical surface
    This kind of versatility makes poufs an easy favourite in any room.

Where should a pouf go in a living room?
While poufs work well in any room, they really shine in the living room thanks to their adaptability. Whether your space is large or compact, there’s a way to make a pouf fit in effortlessly.

  • In front of your armchair or sofa as a footrest
  • Next to your coffee table for informal seating
  • Under a window to create a relaxed reading nook

In smaller living rooms, consider using a pouf as both a footrest and coffee table, saving space without compromising on comfort. Poufs with storage are also especially helpful when every bit of space counts.
